newsitem.title: GERMANY: German grain harvest progresses as rain recedes.
newsitem.headline: German grain harvest progresses as rain recedes.

text.p: Dry conditions this week after excessive rainfall earlier in July will help German farmers continue barley harvesting, the meteorological office DWD said.
"Only little rain is expected this week, mostly in the north but elsewhere soils are drying," a DWD source said.

Barley and rye harvesting was underway in most areas and rapeseed in the south and the south east. Damage from grain lodging was mostly reported in eastern Germany, where farmers also incurred drying costs.
The region also reported rapeseed yields of 3.3-4.0 tonnes per hectare (tph), compared with last year's extremely low pan-German average 2.28 tph.

Eastern German barley yields were reportedly satisfactory and prices might benefit psychologically from flood losses in the Oderbruch region in Brandenburg state, although the affected barley area measures just 7,500 ha.
Wheat, spring grains and oats will be harvested from mid-August across Germany. Sugarbeet was described as flourishing from the additional moisture, which the beet needed after drought in the spring.

Farm sources in Germany's west said between 10 and 50 percent of the barley harvest had been completed in many regions, with moisture below 14 percent. Marketing was slow because there were no buyers and ex-farm prices of 195-210 marks were 20 marks down from last year.
Barley yields varied between 5.00-8.00 tph (tph) versus the pan-German average 5.61 tph last year.
In the north, only 10 percent of barley had been harvested in Lower Saxony. In Schleswig-Holstein, further north, early yields indications were highly promising at 6.5-8.5 tph.
Farm sources in Bavaria said the southern state, which exports grain to Italy and grows malting barley, was expecting a 6.4 million tonne grain crop after 6.7 million in 1996.
This was despite a slight area expansion by 20,000 ha to 1.2 million ha.
The sources cited the spring drought and recent rainfall, which caused delays and volume losses.
Expectations for winter barley were average while those in spring barley, winter wheat, rye, triticale and oats were mixed.

Bavarian spring barley crops may show too much protein to qualify for malting and might need to be sold as feed grain. Bavarian barley yields were around 6.0 tph, with spikes to 7.5 tph and ex-farm prices were at 200-210 marks. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
